title: Beyond Source Code: Evaluating Natural Language Specifications for LLM-Based C-to-Rust Translation
abstract: arXiv:2611.17581v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have shown promising results for C-to-Rust translation, yet existing approaches primarily rely on source code as input, leaving natural-language specifications of program behavior underexplored as an alternative or complementary representation. We hypothesize that direct code translation encourages LLMs to preserve C-specific implementation choices, producing Rust that may be functionally correct but unnecessarily verbose, reliant on unsafe constructs, and less idiomatic. We investigate this hypothesis by comparing three translation settings: code-only, specification-only, and code-and-specification. Using 300 C programs from the IBM CodeNet dataset, we evaluate GPT-5.2 and GPT-4o-mini on functional correctness, maintainability, complexity, idiomaticity, unsafe construct usage, and cost. Code-only translation achieves the highest test pass rate (98.6%) but often mirrors C's implementation patterns. In contras

translated_title: 超越源代码：评估自然语言规范在基于大语言模型的C到Rust翻译中的作用
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）在C到Rust的翻译任务中已展现出可喜的成果，但现有方法主要依赖源代码作为输入，而将程序行为的自然语言规范作为替代或补充表示的研究尚不充分。我们假设直接进行代码翻译会促使LLM保留C语言特有的实现选择，从而生成功能上正确但冗长、依赖不安全（unsafe）结构、且不够地道的Rust代码。为验证这一假设，我们比较了三种翻译设置：仅代码、仅规范、以及代码与规范相结合。我们使用IBM CodeNet数据集中的300个C程序，从功能正确性、可维护性、复杂度、地道性、不安全结构的使用以及成本等方面评估了GPT-5.2和GPT-4o-mini。结果显示，仅代码翻译取得了最高的测试通过率（98.6%），但其生成的代码往往沿用C语言的实现模式。相比之下……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文首次系统评估了自然语言规范作为输入在LLM驱动的C到Rust翻译中的作用，发现仅用源代码翻译虽测试通过率最高（98.6%）但往往照搬C的实现模式，而引入自然语言规范有望生成更地道、更少依赖unsafe结构的Rust代码。
en_tdlr: This paper systematically evaluates natural-language specifications as input for LLM-based C-to-Rust translation, showing that code-only translation achieves the highest test pass rate (98.6%) but tends to mirror C's implementation patterns, while incorporating specifications can yield more idiomatic and safer Rust code.
